summary: Pipe a Readable to a Writable with Node backpressure, event, and destination-ending semantics.

target.notes: Attach destination, enter flowing mode, pause/resume according to write() backpressure, emit 'pipe' on destination, return destination, and by default call destination.end() when source ends.

semantics.backpressure: managed from destination.write boolean and drain

caveats: A simple copy loop misses event ordering, multiple destinations, drain coordination, and error behavior.
options.end === false keeps destination writable after source end.

tests.name: returns destination and ends by default
tests.input: const {Readable,Writable}=require('node:stream'); const r=Readable.from(['x']); const w=new Writable({write(c,e,cb){cb()}}); console.log(r.pipe(w)===w); w.on('finish',()=>console.log('finish'));

tests.name: end false leaves destination open
tests.input: const {Readable,PassThrough}=require('node:stream'); const r=Readable.from(['x']); const w=new PassThrough(); r.pipe(w,{end:false}); r.on('end',()=>console.log(w.writableEnded)); w.resume();
